title: Teeth
objective: After this level you can name the kinds of teeth and what each one does.
summary: Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars grind; 20 baby teeth give way to 32 adult ones. Enamel is the body's hardest substance but holds no living cells, so it can't regrow.

cards.headline: The hardest thing in your body can't heal itself.
cards.body: It isn't bone. It's the enamel on your teeth. It's harder than anything else you're made of, yet it can't repair a single chip. Before we untangle that, meet the tools it covers, because your mouth is where digestion begins.

items.label: Incisors and canines
points: Incisors: narrow edges that cut into food
An adult has 8 incisors and 4 canines

items.label: Premolars and molars
points: Crush and grind food into small pieces
Molars do most of the chewing
An adult has 8 premolars and 12 molars

cards.headline: Two sets, one job
cards.body: Most children have 20 primary teeth, and most adults end up with 32 permanent ones. Every set does the first job of digestion. Chewing breaks food into pieces, while saliva moistens it and carries an enzyme that starts breaking down starches. Digestion is under way before you've even swallowed.

cards.headline: Hard, but not alive
cards.body: Enamel is the hardest substance in your body, about 95 percent mineral by weight, mostly crystals of calcium phosphate. But once formed, it holds no living cells: the cells that built it are lost when the tooth comes in. So unlike bone, enamel can't remodel or regrow. It's also prime real estate. Level 9's Leeuwenhoek first saw bacteria in the plaque from his own teeth.

mascot.line: One coat of enamel per tooth, issued once. Treat it like the only copy, because it is.

options.label: Incisors
options.rationale: They cut into food with narrow edges.

options.label: Primary teeth
options.rationale: That's the childhood set, not a kind of tooth.

questions.explanation: Premolars and molars crush and grind food, and molars do most of the chewing.

questions.prompt: Enamel is the hardest substance in the body. Why can't it repair itself the way bone can?

options.label: Once formed, it holds no living cells
Saliva dissolves any new enamel

questions.explanation: The cells that make enamel are lost when the tooth comes in, so finished enamel can't remodel or regrow.
